items.title: The creation "day" is defined by the equinox sign and lasts about 2,000 years
items.summary: The canon defines the day precessionally but gives no lattice: no word *précession* or *zodiaque*, no 2,160 or 25,920, no count of twelve signs, no BCE date. Landing 25,000 years ago minus six such days gives 13,000 years, the figure book 3 states for the first humans; the canon never states the sum.

items.title: Book 3 prints 666 × 20 = 13,320 years and dates the Flood about 5,000 years ago
items.summary: The multiplication is printed and counted to 1945. The "déluge réel" is placed about five thousand years ago.

items.title: Book 2 corrects book 1 and blames the transcription
items.summary: "il faut rectifier un passage du message que vous avez mal retranscrit": the Elohim will not intervene to destroy humanity. Book 1 still describes the means of such an intervention.

items.title: The Flood's motive and the Elohim's self-discovery differ by book
items.summary: Motive: human progress (book 1); an experiment of little interest (book 2); violence proven by Satan before the council (book 3). The moment the Elohim learn they were themselves created moves likewise. The exiles are pardoned after Babel in book 1 and amnestied before the Flood in book 3.

items.title: The account of Raël's father changes across the books
items.summary: "Étant de père juif" (book 1, Yahweh); "né de père inconnu … paraît-il, un réfugié juif" (book 2); "Celui que tu prenais pour ton père n'était pas ton père" (book 3), with a three-year embargo.

items.title: Proof is promised, refused, then offered by the tempter
items.summary: "preuves incontestables" promised; later "Nous ne vous aiderons jamais ouvertement"; in book 3 proofs are offered in the temptation scene and the mission is described as given without proofs.

items.title: Book 1 ends saying the visitor would not return until the mission was done
items.summary: Book 2 then reports a further encounter in 1975.

items.title: One continent still exists after Babel; the dating argument cites a terrestrial book
items.summary: The scientists are dispersed "sur tout le continent". Book 3's argument against radiometric dating points to *Evolution ou Création*.

items.title: The Babel pardon motive and a non-labour motive for creating man are explicit
items.summary: "afin d'obtenir leur pardon" is stated outright; the evidence map for 0017 grades it as inferred. The canon gives a motive for creating man that is not labour.

items.title: Ellipses inside Bible quotations carry several readings
items.summary: Exodus 14:21 is quoted without the east wind for the "rayon répulseur"; Daniel 10:13 is cut so that Michael helps the Persians; Genesis 7:17 is read against 7:18.

items.title: The Hebrew is sometimes more favourable than the French the canon prints
items.summary: 1 Samuel 17:26 has *elohim ḥayyim* with a plural adjective where the French has "Dieu vivant". The "three stages" of the ark have no noun in Genesis 6:16.

items.title: "Les Clés" (book 2, chapter 3) speaks as a created human
items.summary: The chapter is framed as automatic writing, speaks of "Elohim nos pères, nos créateurs", and has Raël as "je". The library tags it as Yahweh's speech.

items.title: Book 1 narrates five sessions but says six days
items.summary: Four "Le lendemain" frames stand in the text; none at the joins of chapters 3/4 and 6/7.

items.title: Hard prescriptions that the site rarely states
items.summary: Punitive re-creation after death; humanitarianism as "une règle provisoire"; the estate willed to the Guide of Guides; conditional destruction of the State of Israel; killing forbidden even at an Eloha's request, yet execution allowed against a military threat.

items.title: Sendy's books already hold several non-Genesis details
items.summary: Gilgamesh for the ark's cargo ("les semences de vie"); leaders "qui vivent dans les cieux" deciding the destruction; a pro-human Satan.

items.title: The digitised book 1 already reads "Puy-de-Lassolas" and "Mouvement Raélien"
items.summary: Both are points where a first printing may differ.

items.title: Both editions name Dhorme's translation as the Bible used

items.title: The French text of the 13 December 1997 message is in the held 1998 volume
items.summary: Pages 207–210: the preference for Jerusalem was "purement sentimentale"; the request goes to all nations; Israel keeps a short priority.

items.title: Book 3, French 2001 against English 2005: no change of doctrine or figure found

items.title: "Third Temple" is not in the three books; it is Raël's wording in the 1997 postscript
items.summary: The word *temple* never refers to the embassy in the books. Book 1 calls Solomon's house "la première résidence pour l'accueil des Elohim". Claim 0016 records the identification as canon-explicit and cites only books 1 and 2.

items.title: The 2035 horizon is a sum from the 1997 and 2005 postscripts
items.summary: "Dans 38 ans, peut-être même avant" (1997); "no later than thirty years from now" (2005). The numeral occurs in neither the books nor the held volumes; the statement is unconditional where the books make the return depend on the embassy.

items.title: The two 1997 texts differ on where the embassy may go
items.summary: Any nation, and the radius may be water (the message, Elohim's voice); a Palestinian, Egyptian or neighbouring territory, such as the Sinai coast (the postscript, Raël's voice). Book 2 said the alternative country would be near Israel.

items.title: In 1997 the author says he added nothing to the two original texts
items.summary: "Jusqu'à maintenant je n'ai rien ajouté à ces deux textes d'origine." The 2005 English calls itself an updated edition. Only a first printing can test either statement.

items.title: "8 novembre 1991, le jour du Nouvel An Juif" does not match the calendar
items.summary: That day was 1 Kislev 5752; the New Year (1 Tishri 5752) fell on 9 September 1991. Both held editions print the statement.
